claim: In transgenic rTg4510 mice, hippocampal neurons did not fire at specific locations.
source_text: Here we show that in transgenic rTg4510 mice, a model of tauopathies including Alzheimer's disease, hippocampal neurons did not fire at specific locations
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental measurements of hippocampal neuron firing patterns in rTg4510 mice during spatial navigation tasks.

claim: Hippocampal neurons in rTg4510 mice displayed robust firing sequences as animals run along familiar or novel trajectories.
source_text: hippocampal neurons did not fire at specific locations, yet displayed robust firing sequences as animals run along familiar or novel trajectories
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by experimental observations and quantitative analysis of firing sequences in the transgenic mice.

claim: The sequences seen on the trajectories also appeared during free exploration of open spaces.
source_text: The sequences seen on the trajectories also appeared during free exploration of open spaces.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data showing the same firing sequences in both trajectory running and open box exploration.

claim: Hippocampal neurons in the transgenic mice are not primarily driven by external space but by internally generated brain activities.
source_text: The spatially dissociated firing sequences suggest that hippocampal neurons in the transgenic mice are not primarily driven by external space but by internally generated brain activities.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the observation that firing sequences are not anchored to specific locations and appear across different environments.

claim: Tau pathology and/or neurodegeneration renders hippocampal circuits overwhelmed by internal information and therefore prevents them from encoding spatial memories.
source_text: We propose that tau pathology and/or neurodegeneration renders hippocampal circuits overwhelmed by internal information and therefore prevents them from encoding spatial memories.
evidence_reasoning: This is a proposed mechanism based on the observed data, representing a speculative interpretation of the underlying cause.

claim: Alzheimer's disease is behaviorally characterized by cognitive declines such as memory loss.
source_text: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is behaviorally characterized by cognitive declines such as memory loss
evidence_reasoning: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations to Carlesimo and Oscar-Berman, 1992; Salmon and Bondi, 2009.

claim: Alzheimer's disease is pathologically defined by β-amyloid plaques and tau pathology including neurofibrillary tangles and tau-mediated neurodegeneration.
source_text: pathologically defined by β-amyloid plaques and tau pathology including neurofibrillary tangles and tau-mediated neurodegeneration
evidence_reasoning: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations to Wenk, 2003; Ashe and Zahs, 2010.

claim: Tau pathology and subsequent neurodegeneration play a key role in mediating the memory symptoms seen at a mature stage of AD.
source_text: In particular, tau pathology and subsequent neurodegeneration play a key role in mediating the memory symptoms seen at a mature stage of AD
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Ashe and Zahs, 2010 and represents established scientific understanding.

claim: Spatial memories in both rodents and humans are encoded by HP place cells that fire at one or a few specific locations of a given space.
source_text: It is believed that spatial memories in both rodents and humans are encoded by HP place cells that fire at one or a few specific locations of a given space (place fields)
evidence_reasoning: This is established scientific knowledge supported by multiple citations including O'Keefe and Dostrovsky, 1971; Wilson and McNaughton, 1993.

claim: When the animal runs along a novel spatial trajectory, external sensory input at individual locations drives place cells to fire one after another in a unique sequence, which yields a memory code for the trajectory.
source_text: When the animal runs along a novel spatial trajectory, external sensory input at individual locations along the trajectory drives place cells to fire one after another in a unique sequence, which yields a memory code for the trajectory
evidence_reasoning: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations to Wilson and McNaughton, 1993; Harris et al., 2003; Dragoi and Buzsaki, 2006.

claim: A total of 497 CA1 neurons were recorded from eight Tau and six wildtype control mice, all at 7–9 months old.
source_text: We recorded a total of 497 CA1 neurons from eight Tau and six wildtype (WT) control mice, all at 7–9 months old
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct statement of the experimental data collected in the study.

claim: WT neurons fired spikes at stable, specific locations in every lap that the animal traversed a trajectory.
source_text: As expected, WT neurons fired spikes at stable, specific locations in every lap that the animal traversed a trajectory.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental observations shown in Figure 2B and quantitative analysis.

claim: Spikes of Tau neurons were not confined to specific locations.
source_text: In contrast, spikes of Tau neurons were not confined to specific locations
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental observations shown in Figure 2B and quantitative analysis.

claim: Tau neurons' spikes were still specific to one or a few locations in each individual lap, but the locations were changed from lap to lap.
source_text: Close visual inspections revealed that Tau neurons' spikes were still specific to one or a few locations in each individual lap, but the locations were changed from lap to lap
evidence_reasoning: This is based on direct observation of the experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The median lap SI of WT neurons was only slightly (21%) greater than that of Tau neurons.
source_text: The median lap SI of WT neurons was only slightly (21%) greater than that of Tau neurons (Figure 2C; WT 2.03 [1.00 3.09] bits/spike, N = 263; Tau 1.68 [0.84 2.34] bits/spike, N = 262; p=7.7 × 10−11)
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from statistical analysis of the experimental data.

claim: The median trajectory SI of WT neurons was much greater (180%) than that of Tau neurons.
source_text: but the median trajectory SI of WT neurons was much greater (180%) than that of Tau neurons (Figure 2D; WT: 1.29 [0.55 2.61] bits/spike; Tau: 0.46 [0.15 1.29] bits/spike; p=5.3 × 10−39)
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from statistical analysis of the experimental data.

claim: Tau neurons showed much lower rate-stability than WT neurons.
source_text: Tau neurons showed much lower rate-stability than WT neurons (Figure 2E; WT: 0.66 [0.30 0.86]; Tau: 0.075 [0.0042 0.34]; p=1.7 × 10−70)
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from statistical analysis of the experimental data.

claim: Tau neurons lost their overall location-specificity, mainly due to unstable firing locations.
source_text: These results reveal that Tau neurons lost their overall location-specificity, mainly due to unstable firing locations.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the quantitative measurements of spatial information and rate-stability.

claim: A total of 13 template sequences were derived from WT mice and 8 from Tau mice.
source_text: A total of 13 template sequences were derived from WT mice and 8 from Tau mice (Table 2).
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct statement of the number of template sequences identified in the analysis.

claim: A significant number of detected sequences was found for 9 out of the 13 WT templates and 6 of the 8 Tau templates.
source_text: We found a significant number of detected sequences for 9 out of the 13 WT templates and 6 of the 8 Tau templates (p<0.05, Z-test; Table 2).
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from statistical analysis of the experimental data.

claim: The mean Z-scores for all WT and all Tau templates were similarly high.
source_text: The mean (±SEM) Z-scores for all WT and all Tau templates were similarly high (Figure 3B; WT: 2.5 ± 0.3; Tau: 2.3 ± 0.3; p=0.67, one tailed t-test, same below unless specified otherwise).
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from statistical analysis showing no significant difference between WT and Tau sequence robustness.

claim: Both WT and Tau template sequences were detected in almost every lap.
source_text: Both WT and Tau template sequences were detected in almost every lap (Figure 3A).
evidence_reasoning: This is based on direct observation of the experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The mean location shift of the detected Tau template sequences was significantly greater than that of WT sequences.
source_text: The mean location shift of the detected Tau template sequences was significantly greater than that of WT sequences (Figure 3D; WT: 12.7 ± 1.9 cm; Tau: 31.3 ± 6.2 cm; p=0.0035).
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from statistical analysis of the experimental data.

claim: Unlike WT sequences, Tau sequences were not anchored to specific spatial locations.
source_text: Therefore, unlike WT sequences, Tau sequences were not anchored to specific spatial locations.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the quantitative measurement of location shift and visual observation of the data.

claim: The median firing rate of Tau neurons in the open box was lower than that of WT neurons.
source_text: The median firing rate of these Tau neurons was lower than that of WT neurons (WT 1.3 [0.5 3.8] Hz, Tau 0.9 [0.5 2.7] Hz, p=0.0001)
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from statistical analysis of the experimental data.

claim: Firing activities of Tau neurons covered a much larger portion of the box than those of WT neurons.
source_text: firing activities of Tau neurons covered a much larger portion of the box (meaning less location-specific) than those of WT neurons
evidence_reasoning: This is based on observation of the rate maps shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The median open SI of WT neurons was significantly greater than that of Tau neurons.
source_text: The median open SI of WT neurons was significantly greater than that of Tau neurons (Figure 4C; WT: 0.24 [0.04 0.76], N = 131; Tau: 0.11 [0.04 0.34], N = 119; p=1.9 × 10−7).
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from statistical analysis of the experimental data.

claim: Tau neurons fired with low location-specificity in the familiar open box.
source_text: The result indicates that Tau neurons fired with low location-specificity in the familiar open box.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the quantitative measurement of open SI.

claim: Tau neuron sequences, but not WT sequences, during the track running also appeared frequently during the open box sessions.
source_text: it became apparent that Tau neuron sequences, but not WT sequences, during the track running also appeared frequently during the open box sessions
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental observations and quantitative analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: The detected Tau sequences in open box sessions were not due to repetitive running behavior.
source_text: Therefore, the detected Tau sequences in open box sessions were not due to repetitive running behavior.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the Rayleigh test analysis showing no preferred direction in the running paths.

claim: Tau sequences seen in the open box were not primarily driven by spatial locations.
source_text: Together with the low location-specificity of Tau neurons in the open box sessions (Figure 4), we concluded that Tau sequences seen in the open box were not primarily driven by spatial locations.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the combination of low location-specificity and the lack of spatial structure in sequence occurrence.

claim: Tau sequences seen in the open box were the same as those during the track running.
source_text: Even further, these Tau sequences seen in the open box were the same as those during the track running.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on the experimental design where sequences derived from track running were detected in open box sessions.

claim: Tau sequences did not distinguish two completely different spaces during two very different behaviors.
source_text: Therefore, Tau sequences did not distinguish two completely different spaces during two very different behaviors.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the observation that the same sequences appeared in both track and open box environments.

claim: The mean Z-scores of WT and Tau template sequences on the novel trajectories were similarly high.
source_text: The mean Z-scores of WT and Tau template sequences on the novel trajectories were similarly high (Figure 6G, WT: 2.5 ± 0.2, Tau: 2.4 ± 0.4, p=0.91)
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from statistical analysis of the experimental data in novel environments.

claim: The mean location shift of Tau sequences on novel trajectories was greater than that of WT ones.
source_text: but the mean location shift of Tau sequences among laps was greater than that of WT ones (Figure 6H; WT: 9.2 ± 0.9 cm, Tau: 18.5 ± 3.6 cm, p=0.0038)
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from statistical analysis of the experimental data in novel environments.

claim: Tau template sequences were detected in the novel open box sessions significantly more often than WT templates.
source_text: Finally, Tau template sequences were detected in the novel open box sessions significantly more often than WT templates (Figure 6I, mean Z-scores: WT: 0.5 ± 0.2, N = 30 searches; Tau: 1.5 ± 0.3, N = 12; p=0.0029).
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from statistical analysis of the experimental data in novel environments.

claim: Tau sequences seen on the novel trajectories were already preexistent in the prior open box sessions.
source_text: Therefore, Tau sequences seen on the novel trajectories were already preexistent in the prior open box sessions.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the experimental design where open box sessions preceded track running.

claim: The formation of Tau sequences did not primarily depend on spatial experience in an environment.
source_text: These findings suggest that the formation of Tau sequences did not primarily depend on spatial experience in an environment.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the observation that sequences appeared in novel environments without prior spatial experience.

claim: Spatial locations still modulated Tau neurons' firing activities.
source_text: indicating that spatial locations still modulated Tau neurons' firing activities
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the analysis showing that random sliding of rate curves reduced rate-stability.

claim: Tau sequences were trajectory-selective.
source_text: Second, we examined whether Tau neuron sequences were trajectory-selective.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 7 demonstrating differences in sequence occurrence across trajectories.

claim: There was no apparent spatial or temporal periodicity in the occurrence of Tau sequences.
source_text: There was no apparent spatial or temporal periodicity in the occurrence of Tau sequences
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the auto-correlation analysis shown in Figure 8.

claim: The robust firing sequences in Tau mice could not be explained by simple behavioral parameters.
source_text: The robust firing sequences in Tau mice could not be explained by simple behavioral parameters
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the behavioral analysis shown in Figure 9 showing similar behaviors between WT and Tau mice.

claim: Prominent theta oscillations were still present in the CA1 LFPs of Tau mice.
source_text: our data show that prominent theta oscillations are still present in the CA1 LFPs of Tau mice
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the LFP analysis shown in Figure 10.

claim: There was a slight reduction in theta peak frequency in Tau mice compared with control mice during familiar track and open box sessions.
source_text: There was a slight reduction in theta peak frequency in Tau mice (∼8.5 Hz, compared with ∼9.5 Hz in control mice) during familiar track and open box sessions.
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from the LFP analysis shown in Figure 10C.

claim: The absolute theta power was apparently reduced in Tau mice from those of control animals.
source_text: The absolute theta power was apparently reduced in Tau mice from those of control animals (Figure 10D).
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from the LFP analysis shown in Figure 10D.

claim: The normalized theta power in Tau mice was significantly lower than that in control mice only during familiar track sessions, but not during open box sessions or novel track sessions.
source_text: However, the normalized theta power in Tau mice was significantly lower than that in control mice only during familiar track sessions, but not during open box sessions or novel track sessions (Figure 10E).
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from the LFP analysis shown in Figure 10E.

claim: Abnormal theta oscillation is unlikely the cause of the difference between Tau and WT sequences.
source_text: suggesting that abnormal theta oscillation is unlikely the cause of the difference between Tau and WT sequences
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the observation that theta oscillations were qualitatively similar between WT and Tau mice.

claim: The firing stability of CA1 neurons on familiar trajectories in female Tau mice is greater than that in male mice.
source_text: The firing stability of CA1 neurons on familiar trajectories in female is greater than that in male mice.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 11A.

claim: CA1 firing sequences in the transgenic mice become so rigid that they no longer primarily respond to spatial environments or spatial experience.
source_text: Therefore, CA1 firing sequences in the transgenic mice become so rigid that they no longer primarily respond to spatial environments or spatial experience, and therefore no longer capable of encoding spatial memories.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the combined observations of lack of spatial specificity and experience-dependence.

claim: Internal activities underlie the rigid firing sequences in the transgenic mice.
source_text: Therefore, here we propose that internal activities underlie the rigid firing sequences in the transgenic mice.
evidence_reasoning: This is a proposed mechanism based on the observed data and comparison with known phenomena of internally-driven sequences.

claim: When the transgenic mice are placed in a space, instead of forming/retrieving the space's memory code, CA1 neurons are cued to activate those internally driven activity patterns irrelevant to the current space.
source_text: When the transgenic mice are placed in a space, instead of forming/retrieving the space's memory code, CA1 neurons are cued to activate those internally driven activity patterns irrelevant to the current space.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative interpretation of the mechanism underlying the observed phenomena.

claim: The reason why these mice cannot form new spatial memories is because the HP network is dominated by internal brain activities.
source_text: According to this interpretation, the reason why these mice cannot form new spatial memories is because the HP network is dominated by internal brain activities.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative explanation for the memory deficits based on the observed neural activity patterns.

claim: There exists a direct competition between external and internal inputs in HP.
source_text: This interpretation implies that there exists a direct competition between external and internal inputs in HP.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the interpretation of the data regarding internal vs external control of neural activity.

claim: Abnormal external-internal interaction may contribute to memory deficits in neurodegenerative diseases.
source_text: Therefore, our data provide evidence that abnormal external-internal interaction may contribute to memory deficits in neurodegenerative diseases.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations in the tauopathy mouse model.

claim: The non-spatially driven firing sequences were found even when animals were actively moving through space.
source_text: Therefore, the non-spatially driven firing sequences were found even when animals were actively moving through space.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the observation that sequences occurred during movement on tracks and in open boxes.

claim: The external spatial input associated with the movement is overtaken by internal input in the control of CA1 neurons' firing activities.
source_text: In this case, the external spatial input associated with the movement is overtaken by internal input in the control of CA1 neurons' firing activities.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the observation that sequences are not spatially anchored despite occurring during movement.

claim: In Tau mice, tau pathology starts earlier in the cortex including the entorhinal cortex than in HP.
source_text: In Tau mice, there is evidence that tau pathology starts earlier in the cortex including the entorhinal cortex than in HP
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Ramsden et al., 2005.

claim: Within HP, neuronal loss is more prominent in CA1 than in CA3 in Tau mice.
source_text: and within HP, neuronal loss is more prominent in CA1 than in CA3
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Ramsden et al., 2005.

claim: The external input to CA1 through the entorhinal cortex is weakened by the pathology, but the internal input from CA3 is relatively spared.
source_text: It is likely that the external input to CA1 through the entorhinal cortex is weakened by the pathology, but the internal input from CA3 is relatively spared.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative explanation based on the known pathology patterns and the observed neural activity.

claim: Tau sequences are unlikely resulted from periodic firing of entorhinal grid cells.
source_text: Therefore, Tau sequences are unlikely resulted from periodic firing of entorhinal grid cells.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the lack of spatial or temporal periodicity in Tau sequences.

claim: The internal input from CA3, by winning over the external input via the direct pathway from the entorhinal cortex, is the main driving force for producing the rigid Tau sequences.
source_text: Based on these considerations, we propose that the internal input from CA3, by winning over the external input via the direct pathway from the entorhinal cortex, is the main driving force for producing the rigid Tau sequences.
evidence_reasoning: This is a proposed mechanism based on the integration of pathological knowledge and observed neural activity patterns.

claim: Tau sequences mainly reflect the internal information such as old memories stored in the CA3 recurrent connections.
source_text: As such, Tau sequences mainly reflect the internal information such as old memories stored in the CA3 recurrent connections.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative interpretation of what the Tau sequences represent.

claim: There was a trend that Tau interneurons fired with a lower rate than WT ones.
source_text: There was a trend that Tau interneurons fired with a lower rate than WT ones (WT: 24.2 [11.7 46.7] Hz, Tau: 14.8 [8.8 27.2] Hz, p=0.05).
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from analysis of interneuron firing rates, though not reaching statistical significance.

claim: The rate change in interneurons could be one of the adaptive changes in Tau mice to keep the overall activity of remaining HP pyramidal neurons at normal level.
source_text: This rate change could be one of the adaptive changes in Tau mice to keep the overall activity of remaining HP pyramidal neurons at normal level.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative explanation for the observed trend in interneuron firing rates.

claim: The proportion of theta power in the total LFP power is in many cases similar between WT and Tau mice.
source_text: In particular, the proportion of theta power in the total LFP power is in many cases similar between WT and Tau mice (Figure 10E,H).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the quantitative analysis shown in Figure 10E,H.

claim: Theta oscillation unlikely plays a major role in the generation of abnormal Tau sequences.
source_text: Therefore, theta oscillation unlikely plays a major role in the generation of abnormal Tau sequences.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the observation that theta oscillations were qualitatively similar between WT and Tau mice.

claim: The sex difference of Tau mice was previously examined at 5.5 months old.
source_text: The sex difference of Tau mice was previously examined at 5.5 months old
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Yue et al., 2011.

claim: At much older ages (7–9 months) as in our study, tau pathology becomes much more extensive and possibly saturated and thus the sex difference may become less significant.
source_text: At much older ages (7–9 months) as in our study, tau pathology becomes much more extensive and possibly saturated and thus the sex difference may become less significant
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative explanation based on known pathology progression cited from Ramsden et al., 2005.

claim: Stopping the production of the transgenic tau is sufficient to halt the memory deficits at the behavioral level.
source_text: Previous experiments show that stopping the production of the transgenic tau is sufficient to halt the memory deficits at the behavioral level
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Ramsden et al., 2005; Santacruz et al., 2005.

claim: The functional changes at the cellular level in HP identified in this animal model, such as the low location-specificity and rigid firing sequences, possibly also occur in the human brain with similar tau pathological features.
source_text: The functional changes at the cellular level in HP identified in this animal model, such as the low location-specificity and rigid firing sequences, possibly also occur in the human brain with similar tau pathological features.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative extrapolation from the animal model to human disease.

claim: The interpretation that internally generated activities obstruct the formation of new memories is consistent with two typical memory symptoms seen in AD patients: the inability to form new memories and the intrusion of old memories.
source_text: Interestingly, our interpretation that internally generated activities obstruct the formation of new memories is consistent with two typical memory symptoms seen in AD patients: the inability to form new memories (Carlesimo and Oscar-Berman, 1992; Salmon and Bondi, 2009) and the intrusion of old memories (Butters et al., 1987; De Anna et al., 2008).
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference connecting the experimental findings to known clinical symptoms, supported by citations.
